selection_reasoning: Mining a cobblestone wall is a straightforward, observable task that doesn't require deep Minecraft domain knowledge. The agent needs to locate visible cobblestone wall blocks, approach them, and mine them with the provided wooden pickaxe. The task is easily verifiable via inventory check. Single-task benchmark with no dependencies needed.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining a cobblestone_wall block with a pickaxe drops the cobblestone_wall item into the player's inventory. The player starts with only a wooden pickaxe (no cobblestone_wall), so having at least 1 cobblestone_wall confirms the block was successfully mined. inventory_has is the preferred rule type for mine tasks per the design philosophy.

scene_description: A cleared grassy area with a tiered cobblestone wall structure placed 3-5 blocks ahead of the player spawn. The walls are arranged in three rows of increasing width (3, 5, and 7 blocks) at ground+1 level. Trees have been cleared in an 11x11 area to provide unobstructed access. The player is given a wooden pickaxe to mine the walls.
task_text: Mine a cobblestone wall block using the wooden pickaxe in your inventory. The cobblestone walls are directly in front of you.
design_notes: The walls are placed at z+3, z+4, z+5 relative to spawn, forming a tiered structure that's immediately visible. The 11x11 air clearing above the grass platform removes any tree interference. 15 total cobblestone_wall blocks give the agent plenty of targets. The wooden pickaxe is sufficient to mine cobblestone walls (stone-tier, mining level 0). The walls are at y+1 which is eye-level for easy targeting. The pickaxe is auto-equipped in the first hotbar slot via /give.
